correctness.rationale: For k=n the graph is a singleton; for k=1<n it is complete; for 1<k<n<2k dimension forces it edgeless. For k>=2,n>=2k, write U=X⊕A,V=X⊕B with dim X=t and reserve t dimensions outside U+V; a graph of X->Y and A->B is disjoint from both. Quotient lifts containing a vector in V\U give one-sided witnesses, and picking vectors in U and V (or common X plus exterior direction) gives two-sided nonadjacent witnesses. Thus every distinct pair realizes all four third-vertex adjacency patterns, proving rank<=3 Rado equivalence by the 3-move EF game. Three k-spaces in one (k+1)-space sharing a (k-1)-space L defeat the pattern adjacent to only one; the quotient H/U is one-dimensional and any two intersections create a nonzero vector in C∩U. Formula has quantifier rank 4. qK(4,2,2) count [4 choose 2]_2=35. Independently enumerated all 35 2-spaces and all 595 unordered pairs: all four patterns witnessed; pencil obstruction present. The finite check is not proof of every field.
residual_risks: Uniform k>=3 two-point witness is algebraically proven, but a specialist unindexed finite Grassmann-model-theory theorem may already imply the rank-three/rank-four combination.

value.rationale: The first-order logical depth boundary of a natural finite-geometry graph family is a structural theorem with sharp parameter cases and a concrete rank-four obstruction. It is not a textbook translation of ordinary Kneser set families. The 35-vertex minimum makes the threshold checkable without being the entire value.

final_claim: Exactly four quantifier-rank-three theories for finite q-Kneser graphs, with Rado rank-three behavior when k>=2 and n>=2k, and a rank-four pencil obstruction for every such graph.
limitations: Rank<=3 classification, not all rank-four theories; finite field q>=2 and full disjointness, not adjacency Grassmann generalization.
